sources.text: Search this site Embedded Files Microcirculation Laboratory Center for Autodigestion Innovation Our Mission Investigate and minimize Autodigestion as mechanism for human diseases, aging, and death. What is Autodigestion? Pancreatic digestive enzymes have escaped the gastrointestinal tract and degraded your own tissues besides our food. Our Objective Develop new bioengineering tools to identify cellular and molecular mechanisms that lead to tissue and organ dysfunction by pancreatic digestive enzymes. Design new interventions to minimize cell and tissue dysfunctions and destruction initiated and caused by digestive enzymes. Schmid-Schoenbein was born in 1948 in Baden Wurttemberg, Germany, became a U.S. citizen, and received a Ph.D. in bioengineering from UCSD in 1976. After a post-doctoral fellowship at Columbia University, Schmid-Schoenbein returned to UCSD in 1979 as an assistant professor. He developed and confirmed a detailed engineering analysis to understand blood flow in the microcirculation. His research uncovered the mechanotransduction response of white blood cells under fluid shear stress. He discovered the second valve system in lymphatics that is required for lymph fluid from the tissue.

sources.text: Search this site Embedded Files Microcirculation Laboratory About the UCSD Microcirculation Laboratory Microcirculation in the Human Conjunctiva The Microcirculation Laboratory at UC San Diego was founded in 1967 by the late Benjamin W. Zweifach, one of the imminent teachers of Bioengineering and Microcirculation in the twentieth century. In 1979, Geert W. Schmid-Schönbein assumed the directorship of the laboratory. A premise of the laboratory is that diseases are manifest in the microcirculation years before they become evident at the clinical level. The study of microcirculation is a cornerstone for the integration of molecular, genetic, and cellular phenomena with the dynamics in living tissue and whole organs. Microcirculation is a key to analyzing the origin and progression of disease. Report abuse Page details Page updated Report abuse
